# ISS-0001 — Harden workspace selection and application-command authority

GitHub: [#1](https://github.com/digimata/terrazzo/issues/1)

## Summary

The main webview can invoke `set_workspace` with any path and recursively expose that directory through Tauri's asset protocol. The command does not prove that the path came from a user-mediated native selection.

Tauri application commands registered with `invoke_handler` are available to all windows and webviews by default unless the build defines an `AppManifest`. CSP is also currently disabled.

## Evidence

- `src-tauri/src/commands.rs:13-23` accepts a frontend-provided `String` and calls `allow_directory(..., true)`.
- `src-tauri/build.rs` uses `tauri_build::build()` without an application command manifest.
- `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` sets `app.security.csp` to `null`.

## Proposed change

1. Move workspace selection into a Rust command that opens the native directory dialog itself.
2. Do not accept an arbitrary workspace root from JavaScript.
3. Declare application commands through `tauri_build::AppManifest` and explicit capability permissions.
4. Add a restrictive production CSP that permits only bundled application resources, Tauri IPC, and the asset sources Terrazzo needs.
5. Reassess Tauri's isolation pattern before rendering user-authored documents or remote generation output.

## Acceptance criteria

- JavaScript cannot set the workspace root without a native, user-mediated selection.
- Every application command is explicitly granted to the `main` webview through an application permission.
- Production builds have a non-null, tested CSP.
- A test demonstrates that an unapproved path cannot become the active workspace or asset root.

## References

- https://v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities/
- https://v2.tauri.app/security/csp/
- https://v2.tauri.app/concept/inter-process-communication/isolation/
